tldr: Nonlinear response identification from a single noisy treatment can become arbitrarily weak near a straight line. In the exact covariance-preserving Gaussian-latent quadratic model, Theorem~\ref{thm:full-experiment} gives an effective two-way full-likelihood reduction to a curved cubic Gaussian experiment. Theorem~\ref{thm:critical-certified-decision-values} characterizes the continuum minimax causal-slope risk and connected \(90\%\)-honest length frontier by certified finite programs and dual formulas, and Theorem~\ref{thm:critical-original-data-attainment} constructs total data-only procedures that attain it with unknown covariance and exact finite-sample honesty. Supporting results give matching finite-sample rates and the weak no-learning limit, while Theorem~\ref{thm:strong-moving-efficient-attainment} gives efficient positive-curvature moving-law attainment. The contribution is a subfield calibration for CEME uncertainty, with generic weak-identification and decision theory credited.
